bug_semantics: A local attacker who can make tcprewrite process a crafted truncated pcap with `--fixlen pad` can reach `untrunc_packet()`. That function reallocates the packet buffer when the pcap header's wire length exceeds its captured length. If realloc moves the allocation, the pre-realloc base pointer and the IPv4/IPv6 header pointers derived from it in `tcpedit_packet()` become dangling. Processing nevertheless continues through DLT layer-3 merging; the Ethernet L2-length path calls `get_l2len()` and then `get_l2len_protocol()`, which reads protocol data through the freed allocation. The issue #973 ASan trace reports that exact read-after-free and abort path. The defect is the realloc in a control flow that retains aliases into the old allocation, not a bounds error authored in `get_l2len_protocol()` itself.
flaw_origin: Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 is the smallest true BIC. To repair an overwrite reported as issue #80, it changed `untrunc_packet()` to accept `u_char **pktdata`, copied `*pktdata` into local `packet`, and added `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len)` before padding, but it did not make all caller-held aliases safe after a move (and at that point did not even assign the new pointer back to `*pktdata`). Its immediate parent 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e has neither realloc nor safe_realloc in `src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c`, so it cannot free the packet on this path. Commit b58b23a52ffd23c3b1a2e2fe8b868aff0239560d later added `*pktdata = packet`, but did not refresh `tcpedit_packet()`'s local `packet`, `ip_hdr`, or `ip6_hdr` aliases, so the same realloc-caused UAF lifecycle continued rather than being newly introduced there. Commit 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only enlarged the realloc request with `PACKET_HEADROOM`; it is not the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file -p 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14` shows author and committer `Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>` at timestamp 1406047482 -0700 and the complete message `remalloc packets before padding to ensure not overwriting memory - closes #80`; the commit object has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistance, or other trailer and no bot identity.
evidence: Advisory/report: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-722m-c232-cwqp identifies CVE-2025-9386, the `get_l2len_protocol` UAF, affected tcpreplay through 4.5.1, and 4.5.2-beta3 as sufficient; https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/973 gives `tcprewrite --fixlen pad -i POC_tcprewrite_protocol_length_use_after_free_360 -o /dev/null` and an ASan stack in which `untrunc_packet`/`safe_realloc` frees the allocation before `tcpedit_dlt_merge_l3data` -> `dlt_en10mb_l2len` -> `get_l2len` -> `get_l2len_protocol` reads it. Root-cause corroboration: issue #970 reports the same realloc-created dangling IPv4-header alias at another downstream sink, and PR https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/pull/975 says the repair is to avoid realloc because the buffer is already proven large enough. BIC search: `git log --all -S'safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len + PACKET_HEADROOM)' -- src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c` finds only the 2020 size change 64132c54... and 2025 removal 73008f26...; `git log --all -S'packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len)' -- src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c` identifies 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 as the 2014 addition. `git log master -L '/^untrunc_packet(/,/^}/:src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c'` independently shows the 2014 introduction, 2017 pointer-writeback change, 2020 size-only edit, and 2025 deletion. `git show 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 -- src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c src/tcpedit/edit_packet.h src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c` shows the exact realloc/signature/call-site patch. Parent proof: `git grep -n 'safe_realloc\|realloc' 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e -- src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c` returns no match, while the BIC diff adds the realloc; thus the immediate parent lacks this free-and-stale-alias mechanism. Vulnerable-revision flow: at reported revision 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a, `src/tcpedit/tcpedit.c` sets local `packet = *pktdata`, derives `ip_hdr`/`ip6_hdr`, calls `untrunc_packet` at line 262, and later calls `tcpedit_dlt_merge_l3data` at line 354 without refreshing those aliases. Fix proof: `git show 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da` removes `packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len + PACKET_HEADROOM)` from `src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c`, adds `pkthdr.len > MAX_SNAPLEN` rejection in `src/tcprewrite.c`, and bumps `configure.ac` from 4.5.2-beta2 to 4.5.2-beta3; `git grep` on its parent a1778a25a2f8dc4de879782567abab6b923e9694 still finds the realloc at line 575. The direct fix landed via merge a93ae465b966e6f675b25564ce292fb5cfe762ad (PR #975). Ancestry/version checks: BIC is contained by v4.0.5beta1 and v4.0.5, but not v4.0.4; direct fix is not contained by tag v4.5.2-beta2 (which points at its parent a1778a25...), is contained by v4.5.2, and `git tag --contains 73008f...` starts at v4.5.2. This clone has no `v4.5.2-beta3` tag, but the fix commit itself declares source version 4.5.2-beta3, matching the advisory. Marker proof is the exact `git cat-file -p 69831b...` commit object quoted in `ai_marker`.
reasoning: The advisory's named reader is only the observed sink. The causal operation is the conditional realloc in `untrunc_packet`: it may free the old buffer after `tcpedit_packet` has cached the base and header pointers, and subsequent protocol/L2 processing dereferences those stale aliases. History search places the first such realloc in 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14. The direct parent was inspected and has no allocation-moving call on this path, so parent absence is proven despite the parent's separate risk of padding beyond available capacity. The 2017 writeback is an incomplete mitigation, not a fresh origin, because caller-local and derived aliases remain stale; the 2020 headroom edit changes only allocation size. The 2025 direct fix 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da closes the root cause by enforcing the preallocated maximum-size invariant and deleting realloc, with vulnerable beta2 as its parent and fixed source version beta3. Finally, only the BIC commit object is used for attribution: it is a conventional 2014 human-authored/committed commit with no AI marker or bot identity. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
